audits.title: 648 The Use of Antibiotics in Acute Pancreatitis - A Re-Audit of Current Practice
audits.standard: NICE guidance against prophylactic antibiotics in acute pancreatitis; local antimicrobial guidelines
audits.setting: Luton and Dunstable University Hospital, single centre

cycle1.result: Previous audit: 74% of patients received antibiotics without clear indication.

audits.intervention: Recommendations from the previous audit and improved awareness.

cycle2.result: 31 (40%) received IV antibiotics, of whom 14 (45%) had no clearly documented indication.

audits.other_findings: Metronidazole was most used (58%), then amoxicillin (38.7%) and co-amoxiclav (35.4%).
audits.citation: Rai A, Kudchadkar S, Munasinghe A. 648 The Use of Antibiotics in Acute Pancreatitis - A Re-Audit of Current Practice. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.080.

audits.title: 730 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescription in Acute Pancreatitis

cycle1.result: 65.5% prescribed antibiotics on admission; 12.1% for necrosis, 12.14% for concurrent cholecystitis, 33.4% without indication.

audits.intervention: Results and NICE guidance disseminated to general surgery team and at governance meeting.
audits.other_findings: 98 diagnosed, 11 excluded for insufficient evidence of diagnosis.
audits.citation: Othman A, Ben Abdalla M, Baston T, McComb K, Barghash M, Sadic J. 730 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescription in Acute Pancreatitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.138.

audits.title: 706 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing in Acute Pancreatitis and Introduction of a Patient Safety and Cost Saving Diagnostic Tool

cycle1.result: 19/52 (36.5%) with uncomplicated pancreatitis given antibiotics; 22/36 (61.1%) with infection received antibiotics; 36/41 (87.8%) given broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.

audits.other_findings: Trust approved procalcitonin testing in acute pancreatitis after the audit; re-audit planned.
audits.citation: Allen L, Pearman D, O'Connor O, Bagnall M. 706 An Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing in Acute Pancreatitis and Introduction of a Patient Safety and Cost Saving Diagnostic Tool. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad258.364.

audits.title: TPTh 7.07 The Effectiveness of Systematic Interventions Leading to Change in Practice: A Three-Cycle Clinical Audit on Antibiotic Use in Acute Pancreatitis
audits.standard: NICE and BSG recommendations against prophylactic antibiotics in acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: Tertiary upper gastrointestinal surgery unit, Royal Preston Hospital
audits.intervention: Awareness posters after the first cycle, then targeted teaching in weekly junior doctor sessions after the second cycle.

cycle2.result: Antibiotics prescribed in 47.8% (n=11/23); inappropriate prescribing 9.1% (n=1/11) (p for trend = 0.016); documentation of indication 100%.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles: second cycle (August 2025, n=27) had antibiotics in 37% (n=10/27) with 30% (n=3/10) inappropriate. Mean antibiotic duration in the final cycle was 5.3 days.
audits.citation: Mohamed S, Venkatraman S, Mohammed O, Rajendran I. TPTh 7.07 The Effectiveness of Systematic Interventions Leading to Change in Practice: A Three-Cycle Clinical Audit on Antibiotic Use in Acute Pancreatitis. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.497.

audits.title: Antibiotic use in acute pancreatitis: An audit of current practice in a tertiary centre.
audits.standard: IAP/APA guidelines: no routine intravenous antibiotic prophylaxis in acute pancreatitis
audits.setting: Regional Hepato-Pancreato-Biliary Unit, Manchester Royal Infirmary (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: 65 (58.5%) received antibiotics; mean antibiotic use 23.9 (sd 29.7) person-days; tertiary transfers 40.9 (sd 37.1) vs index admissions 10.2 (sd 8.9) days.

audits.other_findings: 31 (28%) were tertiary transfers, who received antibiotics significantly more often; over-use seen in mild acute pancreatitis.
audits.citation: Baltatzis M, Mason JM, Chandrabalan V, Stathakis P, McIntyre B, Jegatheeswaran S, et al.. Antibiotic use in acute pancreatitis: An audit of current practice in a tertiary centre. Pancreatology. 2016;16(6):946-951. doi:10.1016/j.pan.2016.08.012. PMID: 27613614.
